report:
The three sisters moved from a standoff to a shared plan. C opened by saying she would not sign off on A buying the house at a family discount, and that B could use money from the house. A wants the house with her husband at a family discount but wants a way C can agree to. B wants money to start a dance studio. All three said they want a fair arrangement and do not want anyone pressured.

The running list of 11 entries stayed in one place and was shared with each sister as it changed. The main gap was facts: no sister had the will or knew what it said about the house and their shares.

The agreed path is that A and B find their father's will, all three read it together, then they get an independent valuation of the house, and A puts any proposed terms in writing to both of you before anything is decided. A is willing to consider buying at the independent valuation and to take any discount only from her own share. C would consider a sale at the valuation and will not accept a discount that cuts her share. B is open to the same sale once the will, shares, valuation and terms are known. C's last message confirmed she will wait for the will, then the valuation and A's written terms.

Open points: the will's location and contents, each sister's share, the valuation figure, whether B's payout covers the studio, and how long B and C would wait to be paid. No legal advice was given and no money was moved. A will coordinate with B on finding the will.
